title: 44th India Day Parade Marches Through Manhattan as FIA's Guinness Record Legacy Lives On
excerpt: The Federation of Indian Associations' annual parade — the world's largest Indian independence celebration outside India — returns to Madison Avenue on August 16, building on a tradition that includes two Guinness World Records.
body:
• The 44th India Day Parade, organized by the Federation of Indian Associations (FIA) of NY-NJ-CT-NE, marches along Madison Avenue on August 16, 2026, drawing over 100,000 attendees.
  • FIA holds the Guinness World Record for the most different flags flown simultaneously — 826 flags — set during the 2022 parade as part of India's 75th Independence Day celebrations.
  • The parade, running since 1981, has grown from a celebration of 100,000 tri-state Indians to a cultural showcase for over 4.4 million Indian Americans nationwide.
  • More than 1,500 volunteers and over 40 organizational floats participate annually, with past grand marshals including Bollywood and political figures.

Manhattan's Madison Avenue transformed once again into a sea of saffron, white, and green on Sunday as the 44th India Day Parade wound through the heart of New York City. Organized by the Federation of Indian Associations of New York, New Jersey, Connecticut, and New England (FIA), the parade remains the largest Indian independence celebration held anywhere outside India.

The annual event, which traces its roots to 1981, brings together over 100,000 members of the Indian diaspora from across the tri-state area for one of the biggest cultural extravaganzas in American public life. Dozens of floats from Indian-American organizations, marching bands, police contingents, and cultural performances by young Indian-American children fill several blocks of Madison Avenue each year.

A Record-Setting Legacy

The parade's place in the record books was cemented on August 21, 2022, when FIA set two Guinness World Records during the event as part of Azadi Ka Amrit Mahotsav — the celebration of India's 75th anniversary of independence. Volunteers and participants flew 826 different flags simultaneously, setting the record for the most different flags flown at once. The display, which included flags from nations around the world alongside the Indian tricolour, was intended as a show of India's universality and global connection.

That same day, a second record was set for the largest ensemble of the damru, the twin-headed drum associated with Lord Shiva in Hindu tradition. More than 1,500 volunteers turned up early that morning to participate in both record attempts.

"FIA in its own way tried to do its bit by attempting the records and making our motherland shine in our homeland."

— Kenny Desai, FIA President

From 100,000 to 4.4 Million

When the parade began in 1981, it celebrated a milestone of 100,000 Indians living in the New York tri-state area — out of roughly 360,000 in the entire country. Today, more than 4.4 million people of Indian origin live in the United States, with nearly 268,000 in New York City alone. New Jersey is home to one of the largest Indian-American populations in the country, both in absolute numbers and as a percentage of overall state population.

The parade route along Madison Avenue has hosted a who's who of Indian and American public life. Past editions have featured Telugu megastar Allu Arjun as grand marshal, New York City mayors, NASA astronauts, and Bollywood performers. In 2022, a 220-foot-long Indian tricolour made of khadi was flown over the Hudson River as part of the celebrations, and a giant India Day Parade billboard lit up Times Square for 24 hours.

Community and Continuity

FIA Chairman Ankur Vaidya has described the organization's Guinness records as dedicated to the global Indian community. The logistics of such events — coordinating hundreds of flags, thousands of volunteers, Guinness adjudicators, and Manhattan parade permits — require months of preparation.

"The endeavour required massive efforts and the whole team of FIA volunteers worked hard for the past few months, especially since the logistics were a big challenge in itself," said FIA Secretary and Event Chair Pravin Bansal during the 2022 record attempt.

More Than a Parade

The India Day celebrations extend beyond the parade itself. FIA organizes flag-raising ceremonies at Times Square on August 15, cultural galas, and community events across the tri-state area throughout the month. The Empire State Building has been illuminated in Indian tricolour hues in past years, and American businesses — from Dunkin' Donuts to ESPN — have sponsored floats, reflecting the community's growing economic and cultural influence.

For the Indian diaspora in the northeastern United States, the parade has become an annual touchstone — a visible, joyful assertion of identity in the heart of one of the world's most iconic cities.
